blocks.text: Oxidation of organic compounds with oxygen is usually combustion: C2H6 + 2O2 gives 2CO2 + 3H2. Reactions with oxidising agents are also oxidations: ozonolysis is the oxidative cleaving of alkenes with ozone; epoxidation of an alkene is an oxidation using oxidising agents such as molecular oxygen with metal catalysts; and primary alcohols react with acidified K2Cr2O7 to give carboxylic acids, C2H5OH + 2[O] giving CH3COOH + H2O (details in Class XII).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book prints C2H6 + 2O2 giving 2CO2 + 3H2. Combustion gives water, not hydrogen; the balanced equation is C2H6 + 7/2 O2 giving 2CO2 + 3H2O (or 2C2H6 + 7O2 giving 4CO2 + 6H2O).

blocks.alt: 1-Propene, H3C-CH=CH2, with O3 gives the ozonide ring; Zn/H2O gives acetaldehyde (H3C-CHO) + formaldehyde (HCHO), which are reduced to ethanol, H3C-CH2-OH, and methanol, CH3-OH.
blocks.caption: i) Ozonolysis of propene (original drawing after the scheme printed on p268 of the textbook).

blocks.alt: An alkene (H2C=CH2) + O2 gives the epoxide (a three-membered ring of two carbons and one O), which with H+/H2O gives ethane-1,2-diol.
blocks.caption: ii) Epoxidation of an alkene (original drawing after the scheme printed on p268 of the textbook).

blocks.text: Addition of hydrogen to a carbon-carbon double bond to form an alkane is an organic reduction. Various reducing agents are used in organic synthesis, such as LiAlH4, NaBH4 and Sn with concentrated HCl; for example ethanal with LiAlH4, CH3CHO + 2[H] giving CH3CH2OH. Reduction of nitriles to amines, amides to amines, carboxylic acids to primary alcohols and nitrobenzene to phenylamine are further examples studied in Class XII.
